lead: Every physical security key and smart card this realm has recorded. A token is recorded only from its own attestation: today a security key registered with enterprise attestation, whose certificate names its serial. A serial typed by anybody is never recorded. Each token lists the passkeys and certificates on it and who registered them.
capped: This list is the newest thousand tokens. Search by serial or person for any other.
none: No hardware token is recorded in this realm.
lostWhat: Reporting a token lost marks it lost at once, then removes each passkey on it, revokes each certificate on it for key compromise, sends a CAEP credential-change for each and ends the sessions they signed in. A credential that could not be retired is named in the answer and on the audit row, and is still live.
oath.heading: OATH tokens
oath.none: No OATH token is in this realm's inventory.
oath.importLead: The file a token vendor sends with pre-programmed HOTP or TOTP tokens (RFC 6030). Give its pre-shared key, in hexadecimal or base64, or its password. Neither is ever stored. Each key becomes an unassigned token, kept by its serial.
oath.file: The file (paste it, or load it)
oath.what: An unassigned token can be assigned here, or claimed by the person it was handed to: on their portal they type its serial and a code it shows. Its codes then earn the hardware claim hwk while the token is in use. Report the hardware token lost on the first tab to retire it.
enrolNone: This realm's EST issues no PIV slot profile. Add piv-auth, piv-sign, piv-key-management or piv-card-auth to est.allowedProfiles to enrol one here.
enrolWhat: Issue a person a certificate for one of their YubiKey's PIV slots. Paste the certificate request the key signed and, to record the key as hardware, its attestation: the slot's attestation certificate (ykman piv keys attest) and the f9 attestation certificate (ykman piv certificates export f9). An attestation that does not verify is refused.
enrolOptional: The attestation is optional; without it the certificate is issued with no hardware evidence.
escrowWhat: piv-key-management keys this service generated over EST /serverkeygen and keeps sealed under the key-encryption key, so a person's old encrypted mail can be read after a card is lost. Recovering another person's key needs the PIV_KEY_RECOVERY role, which the access-control policy checks, and is audited.
escrowOff: This realm does not escrow piv-key-management keys (piv.keyEscrow). Keys escrowed before it was turned off are listed and can still be recovered.
escrowSearch: Search the Tokens tab for a person to list their escrowed keys here.
escrowNone: No escrowed key is held for {who}.
sshWhat: The OpenSSH user certificates this realm issued to the person, until each expires. Revoking one puts it on the realm's KRL (GET /pki/ssh-user-krl), which the servers that trust this CA read.
sshSearch: Search the Tokens tab for a person to list their SSH certificates here.
sshNone: No SSH certificate of {who} is live.
person.unavailable: This person's tokens could not be read here. Directory → Hardware tokens shows them.
person.noOath: No OATH token is assigned to this person.
person.noYubi: This person holds no YubiKey OTP.
person.yubiWhat: Assign an imported YubiKey to this person by its serial. An OTP typed from the key proves it is in hand and is checked before the key is assigned.
person.sshIssue: A person issues their own SSH user certificate on the portal, for a public key they hold. An administrator can revoke one here.
person.central: Every token in this realm: Directory → Hardware tokens
